reductionFrom.formalDefinition: GRAPHCOLORING = {<G,k> | G is a graph that has a k-coloring}
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: An assignment of labels (e.g., colors) to the vertices of a graph such that no two adjacent vertices are of the same label. This is called a vertex coloring.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the number of colors
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether G has a valid k-coloring
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {((N,E),K) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N, K is int} Example: (({a,b,c,d,e,f},{{a,b},{b,c},{c,a},{a,d},{b,e},{c,f},{d,e},{e,f},{f,d}}),3)
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: {c1,...,cK} | color classes partition N, no edge in E has both endpoints in the same class Example: {{a,f},{b,d},{c,e}}

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Clique Cover = {<G, k> | G is a graph represnted by k or fewer cliques}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: A clique cover is a partition of the vertices into cliques, subsets of vertices within which every two vertices are adjacent
reductionTo.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the number of cliques allowed
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether G's vertices can be partitioned into at most k cliques
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {clique1,...,cliqueM} | cliques partition N, M <= K, each clique fully connected in E Example: {1,2,3},{4,5},{6,7,8}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Clique Cover problem
